nieuw.titel: Avoid taking charges with fragile Wood Elf units
nieuw.tekst: Avoid being charged with your Wood Elf units whenever possible. If you are not confident that you will win the combat, the speaker warns that you will probably lose it.
nieuw.waarom: He describes the Elves as glass cannons: most have Toughness 3 and little or no armour, so attacks that reach them are likely to kill them.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He let a Lothern Skycutter charge his stag-mounted Glade Captain BSB, believing the character could take it. The impact hits killed the Captain before he could attack.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He acknowledges that your units will eventually get caught.

bronnen.citaat: don't get charged if you can help it.

extraCitaten.citaat: you want to be striking first.

nieuw.titel: Prioritise escaping over extra Wood Elf shots
nieuw.tekst: Choose defensive movement over an extra volley when moving will keep your Wood Elves alive. Be willing to march out of a charge arc rather than stand still and rely on shooting to stop the attacker.
nieuw.waarom: He finds that Strength 3 bows often do less damage than expected, while mobility and evasiveness are the faction's strengths.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He describes Glade Guard with an enemy within eight inches: they can test to march out of its charge arc, or stay and shoot, risking certain death if their volleys fail to stop the charge.

bronnen.citaat: you need to prioritize moving and defensive movement

nieuw.titel: Concentrate Wood Elf shooting on one target
nieuw.tekst: Put as many shots as possible into one enemy unit to remove it from the board, then choose the next target. Avoid distributing your Wood Elf shooting across several targets.
nieuw.waarom: He says bringing units down with Strength 3 shooting is difficult, and Wood Elves rely heavily on bows because their magic missile selection is limited.

bronnen.citaat: Try to get as many shots on one unit as possible

nieuw.titel: Spread Wood Elves to prevent chained combats
nieuw.tekst: As enemies approach, spread your Wood Elf units so that catching one cannot lead directly into another combat. Account for the centre-to-centre retreat pivot when checking those paths, rather than simply avoiding placing one unit directly behind another.
nieuw.waarom: He warns that one combat turning into two can cost half your firepower, and that the retreat pivot can create an unexpected overrun path.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He expects something to get caught eventually; the aim is to limit the loss to one unit in a position that does not benefit the opponent.

bronnen.citaat: Make sure only one unit gets caught

extraCitaten.citaat: That can create an overrun path that you might not be aware of.

nieuw.titel: Lure enemies into a corner before sacrificing a unit
nieuw.tekst: Use a unit to draw an enemy into a back corner before sacrificing it. Make the enemy turn around and travel back towards the rest of the battle.
nieuw.waarom: He says this wastes a turn even if the enemy successfully restrains and reforms, letting you focus on other units elsewhere.

bronnen.citaat: If you can suck an enemy unit into the back corner of the board

bron.citaat: Move into the space they occupied.
